summary: Extends Chronicle to display sources as collapsible application groups in the chooser, and renders up to four simultaneously selected sources (from any application) as side-by-side swimlanes in a single transposed calendar view.

classification.why_application: This sprint modifies domain-specific presentation behavior owned by Chronicle: group identity derived from the `application` field, multi-source swimlane layout, and per-source event fetching. All behavior is meaningful only within Chronicle.
non_goals: Group-level selection (checking an entire application group at once)
More than four simultaneous checked sources
Platform extraction of the swimlane or heatmap renderer
classification.not_platform: The swimlane renderer is specific to Chronicle's calendar data model and group semantics. It has no generalization path that would serve other applications without importing Chronicle domain assumptions. Platform extraction is explicitly deferred by the definition.

consumes: shared_views.calendar_event_view (Blueprint) — read-only; fields: date, application, source_label, label, value, selected, detail, deep_link
GET /api/chronicle/calendar/sources — returns list[SourceListRow] in SQL-defined stable order
GET /api/chronicle/calendar/events?application=X&source_label=Y — returns list[CalendarEventRow] for current year
PATCH /api/chronicle/calendar/sources — upserts selection state; request: SelectionToggleRequest; response: SelectionToggleResponse | ApiError
provides: SourceChooser renders sources grouped by application in collapsible sections, collapsed by default, with max-four selection enforcement
SwimlaneRenderer renders 1..4 selected sources (from any application) as swimlane sub-rows within a shared transposed year grid
CalendarPage coordinates multi-source selection state and routes selected sources to SwimlaneRenderer
DayDetailView receives the exact CalendarEventRow for the clicked (source, date) pair — no behavior change
invariants: No transformation, aggregation, or normalization logic exists in the application layer. All value preparation is in the Blueprint SQL view.
Source ordering in the chooser and swimlanes follows the order returned by GET /calendar/sources (SQL-defined). The frontend does not re-sort.
The `application` field is the sole source of group identity. No derived or inferred grouping is permitted.
At most four sources may be selected simultaneously. The chooser enforces this by disabling unchecked rows when selectedCount >= maxSelected.
Selection is global (single-user). No per-user preferences.
Swimlanes within a group are ordered by the SQL-defined source order, not by user action.
SwimlaneRenderer is inline; it has no dependency on any Platform component beyond ErrorCard and Skeleton.
HeatmapRenderer no longer exists after this sprint. CalendarPage must not reference it.
failure_modes: GET /calendar/sources fails: CalendarPage surfaces ErrorCard; no sources are displayed
GET /calendar/events fails for one source: SwimlaneRenderer surfaces ErrorCard for that source's swimlane; other swimlanes continue rendering
GET /calendar/events fails for all sources: SwimlaneRenderer surfaces ErrorCard for each source
PATCH /calendar/sources fails: CalendarPage surfaces an error state; the selection state is not changed (confirm-then-apply — no rollback needed)
Empty selection (no sources selected): CalendarPage shows the chooser with a prompt text and no swimlane area

provides: CalendarPage — top-level React component rendered at route '/' within Chronicle shell entry
SourceChooser — receives sources: SourceListRow[], onToggle, selectedCount, maxSelected; renders grouped, collapsible source list
SwimlaneRenderer — receives sources: SourceListRow[] (1..4), onDayClick; fetches and renders multi-source transposed year grid
DayDetailView — receives row: CalendarEventRow | null; no change from Sprint01

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/chronicle/calendar/sources
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns distinct (application, source_label, selected) rows from calendar_event_view in SQL-defined stable order. No field changes from Sprint01; confirm ORDER BY is in place.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: list[SourceListRow] — explicit stable named contract; Dataset not applicable (no pagination, no row_actions)

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/chronicle/calendar/events
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns all CalendarEventRow entries for a given (application, source_label) for the current calendar year. Called once per selected source in parallel by SwimlaneRenderer.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: list[CalendarEventRow] — explicit stable named contract; Dataset not applicable (sparse date rows, no pagination semantics)

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/chronicle/calendar/sources
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Upserts selection state for a (application, source_label) pair in calendar_source_selection.

internal_flow.name: load_sources
internal_flow.description: CalendarPage mounts and fetches GET /calendar/sources. On success, sources state is populated. selectedSources is derived as sources.filter(s => s.selected). If selectedSources is empty, chooser is shown with prompt text.

internal_flow.name: render_chooser
internal_flow.description: SourceChooser receives the flat sources list and groups them by the `application` field, preserving SQL-defined order. Each group renders as a collapsible section collapsed by default. Sources within an expanded group show a checkbox-style selected indicator. If selectedCount >= maxSelected, unchecked sources are visually disabled and non-interactive.
outputs: onToggle(application, source_label, selected) calls on user interaction

internal_flow.name: handle_toggle
internal_flow.description: CalendarPage.handleToggle calls PATCH /calendar/sources with the new selected state. The UI waits for the response before updating. On success, sources state is updated and selectedSources is re-derived. On failure, sources state is unchanged and an error is surfaced. No snapshot or rollback is needed (confirm-then-apply).

internal_flow.name: fetch_events_per_source
internal_flow.description: SwimlaneRenderer receives selectedSources (1..4). It calls GET /calendar/events once per source in parallel, using application and source_label as query params. Each successful response is stored as a date-keyed eventMap per source. Failures are stored as per-source error state. When selectedSources changes (including year changes), a new set of fetches is issued. No AbortController — prior responses that arrive late are discarded by React state reconciliation.
outputs: eventMaps: Map<string, CalendarEventRow>[] indexed by source position

internal_flow.name: render_swimlane_grid
internal_flow.description: SwimlaneRenderer builds a transposed year grid: rows are weeks (~52), columns are days of week (Mon=0..Sun=6). For each week row, it renders N swimlane sub-rows (one per source). Each cell maps to a (source, date) pair. Intensity class is determined by the value in the source's eventMap for that date: no row = heat-0, 1-25 = heat-1, 26-50 = heat-2, 51-75 = heat-3, 76-100 = heat-4. Month labels appear at the left margin on the first row of each month. Source labels appear at the left margin of the first sub-row in each week block, or as a header row above the first week. While any source fetch is pending, Skeleton is shown. If a per-source fetch failed, ErrorCard is shown for that source's swimlane sub-row area.

internal_flow.name: handle_day_click
internal_flow.description: When a populated cell (value > 0) is clicked in any swimlane, SwimlaneRenderer calls onDayClick with the CalendarEventRow for that exact (source, date) pair. CalendarPage sets selectedDay state, causing DayDetailView to render. Cells with value=0 or missing dates are non-interactive.

internal_flow.name: render_day_detail
internal_flow.description: CalendarPage renders DayDetailView with the selectedDay CalendarEventRow. DayDetailView is unchanged from Sprint01.

risks.impact: Carried from Sprint01: source_label immutability is not enforced. A stale selection against a changed label will silently orphan. No new risk introduced; no mitigation added in this sprint.
If fetches complete at different times, a partial render could flash before all data is ready. Skeleton must be shown until all fetches for the current selectedSources resolve (success or failure).
